clue.text: There's only one in Eire

parts.note: the word Eire has four letters and just one of them, the R, is not a vowel, so the clue describes that kind of letter

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a remark about something unique in Ireland, but it is about the spelling of the word Eire, whose only non-vowel is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter that is not a vowel is the kind Eire contains only once, the R.

clue.text: West Indian going round Cheshire town

indicators.note: the Indian people's name surrounds the other piece, like something circling it

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people, so an Indian in the old Western sense

explanation.surface: A Caribbean traveller makes a tour of a town in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' looks like one phrase meaning Caribbean; split it into West (W) and Indian (CREE). CREWE is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a well-known railway junction town in the English county of Cheshire.

clue.text: In France she can ascend in a flying gondola

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
elle is the French word for she

explanation.surface: A French woman takes off in a balloon basket or airship car.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the passenger car or basket slung beneath an airship or balloon, a gondola that flies.

clue.text: Neat border plant

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one
a lip is the edge or rim of something

explanation.surface: A tidy plant grown along the edge of a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, giving OX.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flowering plant of the primrose family.

clue.text: Put it on without being told?

definitions.meaning: to put on an air or a manner is to adopt it falsely, as with a feigned accent
something taken for granted with no one saying so has been supposed rather than learned

explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means both feigned, as an assumed name, and supposed without proof.

clue.text: Unravel catch line, using a specialised skill

indicators.note: to unravel a tangle is to undo it and rearrange its strands, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to untangle a fishing line, needing expert knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unravel' rearranges the nine letters of 'catch line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical describes work requiring specialist knowledge or expertise.

clue.text: The prosecutor has to act — see foot of column

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
to do something is to act or perform it

explanation.surface: A lawyer is told to take action and look at the bottom of a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot of column' suggests the end of a newspaper article, but it is the architectural sense: the dado is part of a column's pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture the dado is the plain middle section of a pedestal beneath a column.

clue.text: The estate needs me for organisation

indicators.note: the letters are to be organised, that is set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An estate manager insists the property requires them to run it.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord for their own use, an estate.

clue.text: Decide to stop on my own

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off or prevent them acting
something that is mine belongs to me alone

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give something up without help from anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve a matter, to make a decision.

clue.text: Hard task master?

parts.note: read as a master of hard tasks: the Greek hero famed for twelve near-impossible labours

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like 'hard taskmaster', a strict boss; read it as someone who mastered hard tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Greek hero performed twelve famous labours, the hardest of tasks.

clue.text: Brilliant travellers encountered in small firms

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the clue says it is found in the firms

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, so small firms are COS
to have met someone is to have encountered them

explanation.surface: Star salespeople are found working in little businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' suggests talented people, but it means literally shining: comets blaze across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Comets are bright celestial bodies that journey through the solar system.

clue.text: Dispose of at a higher price

definitions.text: Dispose of at a higher price

parts.words: Dispose of at a higher price
parts.note: to get rid of something entirely by selling, read whimsically as selling it upward in value

explanation.definitionFit: To sell up is to dispose of all one's property or business by selling it.

clue.text: Short skirts tempt the clergy!

parts.note: minis are miniskirts
to try someone is to test or tempt them

explanation.surface: Miniskirts are a temptation to priests.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry is the body of clergy, those ordained as ministers of religion.

clue.text: Spots city maze complex

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

indicators.note: something complex is intricate or mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sees an intricate maze in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb, sees; it is the noun, a skin rash. 'complex' jumbles MAZE into ZEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eczema is a skin condition producing red, itchy patches or spots.

clue.text: Inward-looking

parts.note: read literally as eyes turned inward towards the nose rather than introspective

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inward-looking' usually means introspective; here it is eyes literally turned inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a squint where both eyes turn toward the nose looks inward.

clue.text: In control of a race taking two men over fifty miles

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
HE is a man, so two men give HE twice
the second of the two male pronouns
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A motorcycle race is run by two riders over a fifty-mile course.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race. 'over' places the pieces above L and M in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the helm, the steering wheel of a ship, is an idiom for being in charge.

clue.text: Pet cried out, on its last legs

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet animal, old and failing, yelped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'Pet cried'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and feeble from old age, close to collapse.

clue.text: Gathered together and called to order

indicators.note: putting letters to order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: People were assembled and the meeting was brought to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called to order' looks like a stock phrase; 'order' rearranges 'called to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to collect and put pages or information together in sequence.

clue.text: They're not often miscast in Westerns

definitions.text: They're not often miscast in Westerns

parts.words: They're not often miscast in Westerns
parts.note: cowboys throw these ropes skilfully, so they rarely go astray when cast, playing on actors being miscast in films

explanation.walkthrough: 'miscast' suggests actors in the wrong role in cowboy films; it is a rope thrown badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lariats are lassos, long ropes with a noose thrown by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Upbraided a fool, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: tressed hair is braided or plaited

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbraided' reads as scolded; split it into 'Up' (reverse) and 'braided'. A fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a cold pudding of puréed fruit and cream, one example of an after-dinner sweet.

clue.text: Cupboard key

definitions.meaning: a small lockable cabinet for storing belongings
something that secures or fastens, as a key does a lock

explanation.definitionFit: A locker is a storage cabinet and also, literally, anything that locks, as a key does.

clue.text: Prejudiced legal system?

parts.note: prejudiced read as pre-judged: law built on earlier court decisions or precedents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prejudiced' suggests bias; read it as judged beforehand, which describes law resting on precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: Case law is law established by earlier judicial decisions rather than statute.

clue.text: They enter offices uninvited

parts.note: offices here are positions of power such as a throne, seized by those with no right to them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Offices' suggests workplaces and burglars; it means posts of authority taken wrongfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers seize thrones or positions of power without legal right.

clue.text: Minister no longer has an alternative

parts.note: something past is over and no longer current
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A government minister who has lost office now has another option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician; it is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a church minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Dad has to exercise in break

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Father must work out during an interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short break or rest in activity.

clue.text: One of those pieces of eight

definitions.text: One of those pieces of eight

parts.words: One of those pieces of eight
parts.note: pieces of eight evokes pirate coins, but here it means musical compositions for eight players

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces of eight' suggests Spanish coins in pirate tales; read it as musical pieces for eight performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a musical composition written for eight instruments or voices.

clue.text: It lives in Madagascar with the agreement of sailors

definitions.meaning: a nocturnal lemur found only on that island
the naval reply acknowledging an order is yes repeated in nautical speech

explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a Madagascan lemur, and its name is also the sailors' traditional reply of assent.

clue.text: A novice in the actor's union has the same rights

indicators.note: these letters go inside the union's name, as a new member joins it

parts.note: Equity is the trade union for British actors
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A newcomer in the performers' union enjoys equal treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the UK actors' trade union; L is the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality is the state of everyone holding identical rights and status.

clue.text: Matters of give and take between our betters

definitions.text: Matters of give and take between our betters

parts.words: Matters of give and take between our betters
parts.note: betters read as those who bet, for whom give and take refers to prices offered and accepted on a wager

explanation.walkthrough: 'Our betters' suggests social superiors; read it as people placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the ratios offered and taken by bookmakers and gamblers on a wager.

clue.text: Commonsense item worth development

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so these letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Practical sense is a thing well worth cultivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges the nine letters of 'item worth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother wit is native good sense, practical intelligence one is born with.
